bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to housing; creating local government grant account; establishing grant programs for local governments to pay for certain costs of federal action; appropriating money.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. LOCAL GOVERNMENT GRANTS; LEGAL EXPENSES.

Subdivision 1.

Definition.

For purposes of this section, "local government" means a county, home rule charter or statutory city, township, or school district.

Subd. 2.

Local government legal grant account.

The commissioner of management and budget must establish the local government legal grant account in the special revenue fund.

Subd. 3.

Transfer.

On July 1, 2025, the commissioner of management and budget must transfer $10,000,000 from the budget reserve account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 16A.152, subdivision 1a, to the local government legal grant account.

Subd. 4.

Appropriation.

Funds in the local government legal grant account are appropriated in fiscal year 2026 to the commissioner of revenue to make grants to local governments for eligible costs in subdivision 6. The commissioner of revenue may transfer money in the local government grant account to the commissioner of education to distribute grants to school districts that have been awarded a grant under subdivision 5.

Subd. 5.

Application; award.

A local government may apply to the commissioner of revenue for a grant from the local government legal grant account to pay for eligible costs under subdivision 6. A local government may apply to the commissioner for a grant in a form and manner prescribed by the commissioner. The commissioner must allocate grants on a first-come, first-served basis.

Subd. 6.

Grants use.

Money in the local government legal grant account must be used to reimburse a local government for eligible costs incurred by a local government. Eligible costs include actual local government legal costs that were incurred to address the implications of federal executive orders, including:

(1) continuing special education services;

(2) providing programs that reduce disparities;

(3) challenging federal censorship or segregation orders; or

(4) upholding state law that conflicts with a federal executive order that was made effective after January 19, 2025.

No individual grant to a local government may exceed $500,000.

Subd. 7.

Unused balance.

Any balance remaining in the local government legal grant account after July 1, 2026, must be transferred to the budget reserve account by July 15, 2026.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to state government; establishing grant programs for local governments to pay for certain costs of federal action; appropriating money.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. LOCAL GOVERNMENT GRANTS; LEGAL EXPENSES.

Subdivision 1.

Definition.

For purposes of this section, "local government" means a county, home rule charter or statutory city, township, or school district.

Subd. 2.

Appropriation.

$100,000,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of revenue to make grants to local governments for eligible costs in subdivision 4. The commissioner of revenue may transfer money in the local government grant account to the commissioner of education to distribute grants to school districts that have been awarded a grant under subdivision 3. This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2027.

Subd. 3.

Application; award.

A local government may apply to the commissioner of revenue for a grant to pay for eligible costs under subdivision 4. A local government may apply to the commissioner for a grant in a form and manner prescribed by the commissioner. The commissioner must allocate grants on a first-come, first-served basis.

Subd. 4.

Eligible costs.

Grants under this section must be used to reimburse a local government for eligible costs incurred by a local government. Eligible costs include:

(1) increased administrative costs for programs based on federal changes;

(2) amounts for infrastructure projects that have been canceled or withheld by the federal government;

(3) amounts of expected federal funds that have been canceled or withheld by federal executive order;

(4) costs associated with recovery from Operation Metro Surge; and

(5) legal costs associated with upholding state or local laws that conflict with federal executive orders made effective after January 19, 2025.

No individual grant to a local government may exceed $2,500,000.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.
